summary: The sole supplied token is ordinary donkey braying and fits the existing i-a machen sense exactly. Neither the following attack nor beard-pulling is an object or a new meaning of this verb.
The verb has a 3sg masculine L-series ending with the donkey as the sole participant. An agent-like suffix does not require a transitive object; the braying predicate is intransitive in this context.
The current entry already quotes the full 84/54 episode, so no example is added. Its correct Bart wording is not replaced by the supplied translation’s corrupt hart.

The root’s four-consonant shape and initial m- are already filed as stem I in the glossary. Preserve that label and the inherited mzanʕalle/mzanʕər bases; do not move the word to Q solely from a general morphological expectation.
The etymological comparison with nʕr is retained as supplied. One occurrence cannot establish the history of z- or a distinct roaring sense.
Does the contrast between inherited mzanʕalle and source mzanʕarle reflect regular r+l assimilation or a dialectal choice? The current bases and source spelling remain unchanged.
